criteria.rationale: The selected tagment operation consumes previously prepared bacterial or human genomic DNA and prepared transposomes. This is DNA accessible to the reported reaction. Purified genomic DNA rather than native or enriched chromatin is an allowed material-state variation.

evidence.quote: Tagmentation was carried out using previously prepared E. coli (CC118) or human (NA18507) genomic DNA using either 100 or 200 ng of DNA, 5 μl prepared transposomes, 2 μl 5× Nextera HMW buffer (Epicentre), and water to 10 μl.
evidence.rationale: Identifies the actual DNA substrate and its use with prepared transposomes in the selected PCR-free reaction.

criteria.rationale: The selection contains only tagment: coupled fragmentation and adapter joining. The general synthetic-ME reaction describes that coupling; the PCR-free-specific account establishes that the inserted adapters already carry Illumina platform sequences. Upstream transposome assembly and downstream nick translation are outside this selection.

evidence.quote: When free synthetic ME adaptors are used instead (isolated from one another, in contrast to ME-flanked DNA in which two ME sequences are linked by the intervening DNA), transposase activity results in fragmentation and end-joining of the synthetic ME adaptor to the 5' end of target DNA.
evidence.rationale: Directly reports fragmentation coupled to synthetic-adapter end joining.

evidence.quote: We developed a similar approach for transposase-based methods by including sequences corresponding to the primers used for cluster formation, i.e. the Illumina adaptor sequences, into the adaptors that are added during the transposition reaction, as opposed to incorporating them during PCR (See Methods).

criteria.rationale: The paper identifies hyperactive Tn5-mediated oligonucleotide integration and fragmentation/end joining with free ME adapters, and the selected preparation uses Ez-Tn5 assembled with the custom annealed adapters. Exact strand offset and transposase dissociation are not established by these passages and are not asserted.

evidence.quote: In the alternative approach that we characterize and extend here, a hyperactive derivative of the Tn5 transposase is used to catalyze in vitro integration of synthetic oligonucleotides into target DNA at a high density ('Nextera', Epicentre, Madison, WI, USA).

criteria.rationale: The output is genomic fragments bearing transferred synthetic adapters immediately after transposition. NoPCR P1/P2 domains are already in those adapters. Those per-use limitations do not contradict the definition.

criteria.rationale: Both selected operations must be accounted for: tagment couples fragmentation and adapter joining, whereas nick_translate adds a distinct, later polymerase-mediated nick-translation transformation. The source explicitly separates these stages. The whole selected unit therefore exceeds the defined Tn5 transposition operation; the extra operation is not merely a changed enzyme dose, buffer or incubation parameter.

Preservation of inserts and adapters across repair is inferred from the reported resulting libraries and their use to sequence the starting genomes; exact strand replacement and nick sealing are not asserted. This shared information effect does not establish a common mechanism across the two operations.
